valid.code: for (let i = 0, len = arr.length; i < len; i++) { use(arr[i]); }
valid.name: properly memoized length variable, never reassigned in the body - not flagged
unrelated bound (Literal, not a memoized length or a direct .length re-read) - not flagged

valid.code: let len = arr.length; let i = 0; while (i < len) { use(arr[i]); i++; }
valid.name: while loop with a properly memoized length variable, never reassigned - not flagged

valid.code: let len = arr.length; for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) { total += other.length; }
valid.name: loop body reassigns an UNRELATED variable's .length, not the compared memo variable itself - not flagged

valid.code: for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) { use(arr[i]); }
valid.name: unmemoized direct arr.length re-read every iteration - NOT flagged: memoizing measures 1.4x SLOWER at 5,000,000 iterations (TurboFan hoists the read via LICM), so the primary 'must memoize' check was removed

valid.code: for (let i = 0; arr.length > i; i++) { use(arr[i]); }
valid.name: reversed operands (arr.length > i), unmemoized - not flagged, same reason as the direct case

valid.code: for (let i = 0; i < arr['length']; i++) { use(arr[i]); }
valid.name: bracket notation arr["length"], unmemoized - not flagged, equivalent to dot notation

valid.code: let i = 0; while (i < arr.length) { use(arr[i]); i++; }
valid.name: while loop instead of for, unmemoized - not flagged

valid.code: for (let i = 0; i <= arr.length; i++) { use(arr[i]); }
valid.name: <= comparison operator, unmemoized - not flagged, alongside <

valid.code: for (let i = 0; arr.length >= i; i++) { use(arr[i]); }
valid.name: >= comparison operator, reversed operands, unmemoized - not flagged

valid.code: let len = arr.length; for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) { if (use(arr[i])) { total += len; } }
valid.name: memoized variable READ (not reassigned) inside a conditional in the loop body - not flagged

invalid.code: let len = arr.length; for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) { len = arr.length; use(arr[i]); }
invalid.name: "memoized" variable reassigned to arr.length inside the loop body every iteration - defeats the memoization, flagged

invalid.code: let len = arr.length; let i = 0; while (i < len) { len = arr.length; i++; }
invalid.name: while-loop variant of the reassigned-memo bypass - flagged

invalid.code: let len = arr.length; for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) { len = arr['length']; use(arr[i]); }
invalid.name: reassignment via bracket notation arr["length"] - flagged the same as dot notation

invalid.code: let len = arr.length; for (let i = 0; len >= i; i++) { len = arr.length; use(arr[i]); }
invalid.name: reversed-operand (len >= i) memoized test, reassignment still tracked by identifier name regardless of operand order - flagged

invalid.code: let len = arr.length; for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) { if (use(arr[i])) { len = arr.length; } }
invalid.name: reassignment nested inside a conditional in the loop body - still flagged, the check does not require the reassignment to be unconditional

invalid.code: let outerLen = outer.length; for (let i = 0; i < outerLen; i++) { let innerLen = inner.length; for (let j = 0; j < innerLen; j++) { innerLen = inner.length; } }
invalid.name: nested loops, only the INNER memo variable is reassigned - only the inner loop is flagged, reassignment is scoped to its nearest enclosing loop
